items.title: Ashley Keating and Allan Whitworth Interview, 1963-03-22
items.q: What did you think of the, uh, alto player who arrived later, Earl Batiste? ... Uh, he seemed a very good musician.

ctx.x: And then, then the other one arrived later was John Wimbley. That's right. Yes, well, uh, he seemed to have, uh, a particularly good idea of playing second trumpet to me. Mm-hmm. Although from what I've, uh, read on Barry Martin records, et cetera, uh, Eddie Richardson is, uh, allegedly an ideal second trumpet. Uh, but Eddie Richardson to me seemed to be very powerful, and, in, in particularly good lip.

When he was with the Eureka, he's the guy who carried the melody with him, you know. Yeah. Not, not second trumpet. No, he, and with this he's, man, he's more featured. That's right. Yeah, so it would appear that way. Yeah, well, they have, uh, a funny kind of setup in the New Orleans brass band trumpet. There's no point in going into that now. Uh, let's see. What did you think of the, uh, alto player who arrived later, Earl Batiste?

Uh, he seemed a very good musician. Uh, being a dyed in the wool, uh, Bunk Johnson and Lewis fan, uh, to be quite frank, no saxophone, uh, really moves me. Although, uh, having heard Manuel Paul, uh, play tenor, I found that quite interesting. Uh, but this, uh, lad was obviously a good musician. There's no two ways about that. Again, he played with a fairly strong vibrato. Uh, I would have liked to have heard him on some other instrument. I think you suggested to him, he might perhaps like to play a soprano or a…
